common_name: Party Time Alternanthera (Pink and Green Splashed Joseph's Coat)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery transplants after the soil has warmed well past the last frost, into humus-rich, well-drained soil in bright light. Party Time's variegated color is strongest with several hours of direct or very bright indirect sun.

directions: Party Time is the older, variegated parent form behind several later solid-colored calico plant sports, and it is grown for wavy-edged leaves splashed unevenly in green, pink, magenta, and cream rather than a single uniform hue. Because the pink and cream patches are the result of natural chimeral variegation, propagate only from cuttings taken from strongly patterned stems, since all-green reversion shoots that appear on a plant should be pinched out before they take over. Grow it in a hanging basket, mixed container, or as a fine-textured edging plant where the shifting, mottled pattern reads as a soft color blend rather than the bold solid blocks of newer alternanthera cultivars. Pinch tips regularly through the season to keep growth dense and to encourage fresh, more vividly colored new leaves.

common_name: True Yellow Alternanthera (Golden Fine-Leaf Joseph's Coat)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or transplants once night temperatures stay reliably above 55°F, in average, well-drained soil in full sun to bright partial shade. Full sun deepens True Yellow's gold color; shadier spots keep new growth more chartreuse-green.

directions: True Yellow stands apart from the burgundy- and red-leaved alternantheras that dominate the genus, producing narrow, glossy, chartreuse leaves that mature to a bright, almost luminous gold — a rare true-yellow foliage tone useful for lighting up shady containers or edging beds of darker foliage plants. Its low, dense, mounding habit stays compact without regular shearing, though light tip-pinching early in the season encourages fuller branching and more leaf surface for color display. Pair it with burgundy or near-black companions such as Persian shield or dark-leaved coleus for maximum contrast. Take stem cuttings in late summer to overwinter stock plants indoors under bright light, since this cultivar does not come true from seed.

common_name: Choco Chili Alternanthera (Black-Top Ruby-Backed Joseph's Coat)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade. Choco Chili's naturally compact, well-branched habit needs little pinching to stay full in containers or beds.

directions: Choco Chili is a modern patented hybrid selected for a striking bicolor leaf, nearly black-purple on the upper surface and a contrasting bright ruby-red beneath, so the foliage flashes color as leaves shift and arch in the breeze. Its vigorous, self-branching, slightly trailing habit spills gracefully over the rim of a pot or hanging basket without becoming leggy, making it a strong thriller-adjacent filler in mixed summer combinations. Foliage darkens to its richest near-black tone in full sun and stays more purple-green in shadier spots, so give it as much light as the surrounding planting allows. Because it is a patented hybrid, propagate only vegetatively from cuttings and bring stock plants indoors under bright light before the first fall frost to carry them over winter.
